info.name: CROIP Central Platform API
info.description:
Central Revenue Oversight & Integration Platform — all 11 microservice APIs, organized by WHO calls them rather than which service owns them:

- **1. Ratepayer** — citizen self-service: self-register a profile directly through a concession's own app (identified by that concession's public, non-secret code — never its real API credential), log in (password + OTP), read/update own profile, claim an existing unclaimed property, own bills/disputes, receipt verification. A concession's staff can also register/update a ratepayer on their behalf, walk-in style — that path is concession-scoped (see below). Once a profile exists (either way), login, profile read/update, and claims all work unscoped, across any concession — a ratepayer with property in two different MMDAs only ever needs one account.
- **2. Concession** — revenue-collection partner field staff: walk-in ratepayer registration/update/delete, property registration/verification in the field, billing and payment collection, event reporting, reference-data lookups.
- **3. CROIP Admin** — central platform/oversight staff: user & RBAC management, concession onboarding, reconciliation, audit, boundary/reference-data management, review/approval steps.
- **Platform Health Checks** — infra liveness/readiness, not tied to any persona.

Some endpoints are genuinely cross-cutting (e.g. a property verification is *submitted* by Concession staff but *reviewed* by CROIP Admin) — each lives under the persona who actually calls that specific endpoint, with a note where the split matters.

**Auth model**
- Ratepayer: no auth for self-register/login/claims/receipt-verification; phone/email + password + OTP issues `{{ratepayer_access_token}}` (HS256, ratepayer-service) for login, own-profile read/update, and claims — it is not accepted for a walk-in staff registration/update, or any property-registry-service endpoint.
- Concession & CROIP Admin: both use the same real Zitadel-issued `{{staff_access_token}}` (RBAC permissions, plus a concession-ownership check on walk-in ratepayer update/delete, decide what each officer can actually do) — there's no API-only login by design; sign into the portal (http://localhost:3050) as a real officer and copy the access token (see README).

item.name: Auth & Profile
item.description: ratepayer-service — citizen login, self-registration, and own-profile read/update/delete, all unscoped across any concession once the profile exists. A concession's staff can also register or update a ratepayer on their behalf, walk-in style (see 2. Concession > Ratepayers) — that path stays concession-scoped.

item.name: Look up a concession by its public code

request.description: No auth — a concession's own public ratepayer-facing app calls this with its plain, non-secret code (never its real API client credential) to find the concessionId to pass to self-registration. Returns only {id, code, name, status}.

No auth — a ratepayer creates their own profile directly through a concession's public app, instead of needing to walk into an MMDA office. concessionCode identifies which concession this profile belongs to (resolved via the by-code lookup above). Once created, login works across every concession's app, same as a staff-registered profile. Registering with an email sends a real OTP to Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) — check there and paste the code into ratepayer_otp_code; it's no longer echoed in the response. Use a phone number instead of email (no email field) to get devOtpCode back automatically, since SMS has no real provider wired up yet. The email is white-labeled as the concession (its name as the sender/subject/header) — a ratepayer never sees any CROIP branding; falls back to a neutral 'Ratepayer Services' label only if no concession is on file. Also accepts an optional idempotencyKey — see '2. Concession > Register a ratepayer (walk-in)' for what it's for.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set('ratepayer_id', j.id); if (j.otp && j.otp.devOtpCode) pm.environment.set('ratepayer_otp_code', j.otp.devOtpCode); }

request.description: Email OTPs are dispatched to a real inbox in Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) and are deliberately NOT echoed back in the response — copy the code from there into ratepayer_otp_code. Phone OTPs still come back as devOtpCode (auto-saved by this request's test script) since there's no real SMS provider wired up yet. White-labeled as the ratepayer's own concession, never CROIP.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { const j = pm.response.json(); if (j.devOtpCode) pm.environment.set('ratepayer_otp_code', j.devOtpCode); }

item.name: Login step 2: verify OTP → session token

request.description: Revokes just this session token server-side (not every session this ratepayer has elsewhere) — every subsequent request with {{ratepayer_access_token}} now gets 401 Invalid or expired access token, same as a naturally-expired one. Run Login step 1+2 again to get a fresh token.

item.name: Forgot password step 1: send reset OTP

request.description: No auth, no password required — this is the "I forgot it" flow. Always returns the same OTP_REQUIRED shape whether or not the identifier is registered; only a real account actually gets an OTP generated and dispatched. Email OTPs go to Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) and are not echoed back — check there; phone OTPs still come back as devOtpCode since there's no real SMS provider yet.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { const j = pm.response.json(); if (j.devOtpCode) pm.environment.set('ratepayer_otp_code', j.devOtpCode); }

item.name: Forgot password step 2: verify OTP → set new password

request.description: Confirms the PASSWORD_RESET OTP (a distinct purpose from login/registration OTPs — one can never be replayed as the other), sets the new password, and immediately issues a session token — same as a normal login, since this proves account ownership just as well.

Uses the ratepayer's own {{ratepayer_access_token}}, not a concession credential — unlike '2. Concession > Update a ratepayer profile', this is never rejected for cross-concession ownership. Extensive: every self-owned field can be changed (name, ratepayerType, phone, address, coordinates/MMDA, password) except email, the concession registered with, and other immutable fields (code, id, status) — sending any of those is rejected with 400, not silently ignored.

Every real action taken on my own account (registered, logged in, profile updated, KYC submitted, password reset, etc.), most recent first — the same chronological log CROIP staff see on my profile's Account Activity card, scoped to just me.

item.name: Verify KYC for own profile (Bearer token)

request.description: Verify KYC on own signed-in account using Bearer token. Supported providers: GHANA_CARD, PASSPORT, DRIVERS_LICENSE. Choosing a new provider archives previous verifications for audit trail.
Verify ratepayer using Ghana Card (NIA). Format: GHA-XXXXXXXXX-X. Choosing a new provider archives any previous active verification.
Verify ratepayer using Passport. Format: GXXXXXXXX. Archives previous Ghana Card verification for audit trail.
Verify ratepayer using Driver's License (DVLA). Format: DL-XXXXXXXX-X. Archives previous Passport verification for audit trail.

Self-service account deletion — same business rule as the concession-mediated delete in '2. Concession > Ratepayers' (rejected with 400 if any properties are still linked; sever those first), just scoped to my own account via {{ratepayer_access_token}} instead of a concessionId.

item.name: Properties
item.description: property-registry-service — a concession's field agents registering and verifying properties in their assigned MMDAs. Uses {{concession_access_token}} throughout (mint it first under 'API Clients (self-service)'), except field verification itself which genuinely needs {{staff_access_token}}.

request.description: Use {{concession_access_token}} — this is the token minted from your client_id/client_secret (see 'Mint access token' above). The concession is identified from that token, not the request body. Concessions can only register properties whose polygon falls strictly within their assigned MMDA territory (enforced via Shared Services and Platform Governance). Spatial non-overlap restriction: polygons cannot overlap or contain another property parcel when property uses and ownership percentage match. Core classification fields are required; propertyName and documents are optional.

Use {{concession_access_token}}. Batch registration (up to 500 properties). All properties must fall within the concession's assigned MMDA boundary. Core classification fields are required for each property; code is generated if omitted; propertyName and documents are optional.

item.name: Update property - metadata only (preserves valuation & status)

request.description: Use {{concession_access_token}}. Non-structural updates preserve valuations and verification status.

item.name: Update property - structural / usage change (resets to UNASSESSED, decouples valuation)

request.description: Use {{concession_access_token}}. Updates physical structure or property use (e.g. building renovation, repurposing, adding floors). Automatically marks property UNASSESSED, resets verificationStatus to PENDING, and decouples active valuations pending re-assessment.

Needs 'properties:verify', which is NOT among a concession API client's granted permissions (by design — a concession can't self-verify its own registrations) — this one genuinely requires {{staff_access_token}}, unlike the rest of this folder. Reviewed/approved afterwards by CROIP Admin (see that folder's Property Oversight section).

Use {{concession_access_token}}. Strictly rejected with 400 Bad Request if any bills on this property have been paid (in which case only ratepayer links can be severed). If eligible for deletion, automatically severs all ratepayer links in ratepayer-service and cascades units, valuations, documents, and photos.

item.name: Ratepayers
item.description: ratepayer-service — ratepayer registration, update, and delete are concession-mediated: use {{concession_access_token}} (minted from the concession's own client_id/client_secret, not {{staff_access_token}}), since which concession a ratepayer belongs to is read from that token, not the request body. Update/delete are rejected with 403 for a ratepayer not registered by this concession. Ratepayer login, own-profile read, and claims stay unscoped (see 1. Ratepayer).

request.description: Use {{concession_access_token}}. Same directory endpoint CROIP staff use, granted to a concession's own API client via ratepayers:read (the same shape of grant properties:read already gives it for GET /properties) — not automatically scoped to only this concession's own ratepayers, matching how properties:read already works platform-wide rather than per-assembly.

Use {{concession_access_token}} — the ratepayer's concessionId is taken from the caller's own token's client_id, never from the request body. A staff token also technically works (CROIP Admin can register on a concession's behalf) but falls back to a shared default concessionId rather than a real one, so it doesn't actually demonstrate which concession owns this ratepayer — use the concession's own token to test that for real. Accepts all ratepayer profile fields; only email (or phone number) and password (with confirmPassword) are strictly required. Since both email and phone are set here, the OTP goes to email (Mailpit, http://localhost:8025, not echoed in the response) — clear the email field to test the phone/SMS path with devOtpCode auto-filled instead. Optional idempotencyKey makes this safe to retry — e.g. a field agent registering a ratepayer with no signal, whose app generates the key once offline and resends the same request (same key, same body) once connectivity returns: a retry replays the original 201 response instead of creating a duplicate; the same key with a different body is rejected with 409.

Use {{concession_access_token}}. Rejected with 403 if this ratepayer was registered by a different concession than the caller's token. Used to complete missing profile sections or update any field; omitted/updated fields immediately update completion metrics.

Use {{concession_access_token}}. Rejected with 403 if this ratepayer was registered by a different concession than the caller's token, or 400 Bad Request if the ratepayer has linked properties. To delete a ratepayer, first sever all property links or delete unbilled properties.

item.name: API Clients (self-service)
item.description: platform-governance-service — a concessionaire managing its OWN API credential with its own current Bearer token (concessionId comes from that token, never a URL param, so you can only ever touch your own credential). CROIP provisions the first one at onboarding (see 3. CROIP Admin > Concession Management); this is what you integrate into your own system afterward.

request.description: Mints a bearer token as this concessionaire's own API client, for the self-service requests below. Grant type: client_credentials.
Never includes secrets — those are shown once, at issuance time.
Revokes your current credential at Zitadel and issues/emails a new one. You can never have two active credentials at once, so do this as soon as you suspect the current one is compromised.
Revokes your current credential without issuing a replacement — you will need CROIP staff to re-provision one if you have no other way to authenticate afterward.

Admin purge all partner concessionaires, assigned contracts, field personnel, and API clients. Strictly preserves the superuser account (superuser@croip.com) and SUPER_ADMIN RBAC role.
Admin purge all citizen & corporate ratepayer profiles, verifications, OTPs, and property claims. MMDA boundaries remain completely untouched.
Admin purge all property bills, payment links, and payment transaction records.
Admin purge all disputes, evidence files, and comments.
